To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present Compositional attention networks for machine reasoning, a novel neural architecture that is designed to support explicit and expressive reasoning, which we demonstrate to be effective on the challenging CLeVR dataset for visual question answering.

1) Compositional Attention Network (CAN) models are more efficient, robust and data-efficient than monolithic black-box neural network architectures; and 2) CANs are a promising new class of neural network architectures that can be applied to other tasks and datasets.

(1) we propose a novel fully differentable neural network architecture for machine reasoning that provides a strong inductive bias for structured reasoning, enabling it, among other benefits, to achieve state-of-the-art performance with an order of magnitude fewer parameters and less training data, and (2) we demonstrate the strength and robustness of the model on a challenging visual reasoning dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of neural networks that can be used to learn and reason in a way that is more human-like and interpretable.
developing a new class of neural network architectures, Compositional Attention Models, that are designed to facilitate explicit reasoning, and to enable explainable and structured machine learning.
the design of neural network architectures that support explicit, explainable, and structured learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our model is the first neural architecture for visual reasoning that combines the best of both worlds: it is as strong as the best black-box neural networks in terms of performance, but also as explainable and data-efficient as symbolic AI systems.
the model provides a strong prior on iterative reasoning, enabling explainable and structured reasoning, as well as data-efficient generalization from a small amount of data.

our compositional attention networks for machine reasoning are a new state-of-art method for visual reasoning, and that they achieve a 98.9\% accuracy, halve the error rate of previous models, and are computationally efficient, and require an order of magnitude fewer resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new architecture is a step towards building neural models with explicit control, which can learn and generalize from a modest amount data.
we propose a new architecture for machine reasoning, which is able to achieve state-of-the-art results on the CLEVR dataset, and is significantly more data efficient than existing models.
we have proposed a novel architecture, Compositional Attention Network, that is able to learn to reason by explicitly modeling attention, memory, and control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by designing neural networks to incorporate a strong prior for explicit and structured reasoning, we can achieve better generalization from a small amount of data.
the explicit control of attention and memory, and the ability to reason about the structure of a problem, are key ingredients in the design of neural networks for machine reasoning.

explicit control and attention mechanisms can be incorporated in neural networks in an efficient, modular, and scalable fashion, enabling the design of models that support structured reasoning and explainability.
